description: DNS bandwidth amplification (de-probabilised, after Deshpande-Katsaros-Basagiannis-Smolka HASE 2011). Faithful elements: a bandwidth queue of capacity BQUL, an amplification factor EAF (each unblocked bogus request costs EAF), a server drain `serve`, and a bounded filtering countermeasure `fcap`. The attacker (coalition) can drive the queue past capacity -> expected TRUE, matching the paper's central finding that the amplification attack succeeds (attack probability -> 1) against any finite provisioning. The defender's capacity/filtering (adversary, bounded) only mitigates. Abstracts the probabilities/rates and the cost-benefit reward analysis.
